sections.label: LPA registrations and fee waiver
sections.summary: Over 120,000 LPAs were registered by May 2021, and the $75 fee for LPA Form 1 by Singapore Citizens is waived until March 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Already, we have more than 120,000 LPAs registered as of May 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To encourage more Singaporeans to sign up and pre-plan, we have waived the $75 fee for LPA Form 1 applications by Singapore Citizens until March 2023.

sections.label: New electronic transaction system OPGO
sections.summary: Clause 3 introduces a new Part IIIA on the establishment and operations of a new electronic transaction system, OPG Online or OPGO.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Clause 3 of the Bill introduces a new Part IIIA on matters pertaining to the establishment and operations of a new electronic transaction system, OPG Online or OPGO.

sections.label: Online LPA processing and objections
sections.summary: Most online LPA applications can be processed immediately, but a three-week waiting period still allows objections to registration.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: With built-in system checks and validations, most online LPA applications can be immediately processed upon submission.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This is a substantial time saving compared to the current three weeks processing time.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To be clear, there will still be a three-week waiting period allowing for any objection to the registration of the LPA to be raised.

sections.label: 90-day period for errors
sections.summary: Under new sections 11(7) and 11(12), a 90-day notice period applies, after which the electronic copy is treated as the LPA if no error is notified.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Under the new section 11(7), they will be given 90 days after the date of notice to notify the Public Guardian of any error.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Under the new section 11(12), if the Public Guardian is not notified of an error, the electronic copy will be treated as the LPA after the end of the 90-day period.

sections.label: Protection for donees and third parties
sections.summary: New section 16A protects a donee who relied on an erroneous electronic copy unknowingly and a third party who transacted in good faith.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: In the unlikely event that there is an error in the electronic copy, the new section 16A of the Act which is inserted by clause 10 of the Bill, protects the donee if he or she had relied on the electronic copy without knowing of the error and protects any third party, if the third party had transacted in good faith and without knowledge of the error.

sections.label: Public Guardian interviews for suspected fraud
sections.summary: New section 31A allows the Public Guardian to interview the donor and disclose information if fraud or undue pressure is suspected.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To safeguard against such risks, the new section 31A of the Act, which is inserted by clause 12 of the Bill allows the Public Guardian to interview the donor and disclose certain information if she suspects that fraud or undue pressure has been used to induce the donor to make an LPA or appoint a person to be his or her donee.

sections.label: Public Guardian fraud investigation powers
sections.summary: The Public Guardian may apply to the Court to determine if a suspected fraudulent LPA should remain registered, but this does not apply retrospectively.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Further, if the Public Guardian has reason to suspect that fraud or undue pressure has indeed taken place, she may exercise her supervisory and investigative functions, for instance, by applying to the Court under the existing section 17 of the Act to determine if the LPA should still be registered.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This amendment will not apply retrospectively to LPAs registered prior to the amendment.

sections.label: Donees are immediate family
sections.summary: Almost 90% of donees are the donor's immediate family members, and more than 60% of them are below 50 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Today, almost 90% of the donees are the donor's immediate family members, of which more than 60% are below 50 years old.

sections.label: Bill establishes electronic LPA process
sections.summary: The Bill amends the MCA to establish a simplified electronic process for creating Lasting Powers of Attorney, which let individuals appoint decision-makers if they lose mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We will walk this journey with our citizens to ensure that everyone can take advantage of OPGO and it is my hope that Singaporeans will leverage this digital transformation to make their LPAs safely, conveniently and expediently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This Bill amends the MCA so as to establish a simplified electronic process for the creation of Lasting Powers of Attorney, which allow individuals to appoint persons to make decisions on their behalf should they lose their mental capacity to do so themselves.

sections.label: Few seniors made LPAs
sections.summary: As of 2018, only about 23,000 Singaporeans above 65 had made their LPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As of 2018, only about 23,000 Singaporeans above 65 have made their LPA.

sections.label: Amendments remove physical meetings
sections.summary: The current process requires hardcopy documents and physical meetings between donor and donee, but the amendments remove the need to meet physically to sign and exchange documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Currently, the process requires the hardcopy of all documents and physical meetings between donor and donee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With the amendments, parties do not need to physically meet up to sign and exchange documents.

sections.label: Default setting versus active consent
sections.summary: The proposal treats the e-copy of the registered LPA as free from error if no error is notified within 90 days, but the speaker prefers affirmative confirmation by the donor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Additionally, the current proposal's "default setting" is to treat the e-copy of the registered LPA in OPGO as free from error and as the LPA if there is no notification of any error within 90 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: While this method might be administratively expedient and help save time, and certainly it does, given that this is such an important document, I think we should instead make it an affirmative confirmation by the donor that all details are correct; that is, to ensure that the consent is active consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In such cases, the Public Guardian can disclose to the donor the number of LPAs for which their prospective donee has already been appointed to allow them to make a more informed decision.

sections.label: Disclosure of multiple nominee donee
sections.summary: The passage states that where the donee is a multiple nominee, this must be disclosed to the donor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Instead, as long as the donee is a multiple nominee, I think this must be disclosed to the donor.

sections.label: Support for online LPA Bill
sections.summary: A court-appointed deputy supports the Bill, saying it makes executing and registering LPAs more convenient than printing and submitting wet-ink documents to the OPG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have also had personal experience as a court-appointed deputy of a mentally incapacitated person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am generally in support of this Bill, which promises to make it more convenient for the public to execute LPAs and register them instead of needing to print and submit wet-ink documents to the OPG.

sections.label: Donor appearance before Certificate Issuer
sections.summary: Even with the move online, the Ministry decided to retain the requirement for an LPA donor to appear in person before the Certificate Issuer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even if the move is to go online, the Ministry has decided to retain the requirement for an LPA donor to appear in person before the Certificate Issuer.

sections.label: Public Guardian requiring donor appearance
sections.summary: New section 31A lets the Public Guardian require the donor to appear if there is reasonable cause to suspect fraud or undue pressure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The new section 31A provides that the Public Guardian may require the donor to appear before him if there is reasonable cause to suspect that fraud or undue pressure was used to induce the donor to execute the LPA or to appoint a particular donee.

sections.label: Multiple LPA donee as suspicious
sections.summary: The Bill specifically suggests that being a donee in multiple LPAs is a suspicious circumstance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, the Bill specifically suggests that being a donee in multiple LPAs is a suspicious circumstance.

sections.label: Online LPA registration amendments
sections.summary: The amendments provide for LPAs to be made and registered online via OPGO, to cope with rising volume, speed the process and store, search and retrieve electronic LPAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The amendments primarily provide for Lasting Power of Attorney (LPAs) to be made and registered online through the formation of an what the Parliamentary Secretary calls OPGO, an Office of the Public Guardian Online electronic system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There are good reasons for this change: (a) to cope with the rising LPA volume, which has increased nine-fold from 2,681 in year 2014 to close to 25,000 in 2019; (b) to enable a faster and more convenient process – the change removes the need to physically print and submit hardcopies or affix wet-ink seals and signatures currently need for LPA deeds; (c) and the third good reason, the proposed amendments provide for new features to better store, search and retrieve electronic LPAs versus hard copy LPAs.

sections.label: Dementia among Singapore elderly
sections.summary: A 2015 IMH-led WiSE study found one in 10 people aged 60 and above may have dementia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In a 2015 study conducted by the Well Being of the Singapore Elderly or WiSE led by the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), one in 10 people aged 60 and above may have dementia.

sections.label: Internet use among older residents
sections.summary: An IMDA 2019 survey found 58% of residents above 60 are Internet users versus 89% of all residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In an IMDA survey of 2019, it was revealed that 58% of residents above age 60 are Internet users compared to 89% for all residents – a percentage-point difference of about 30%.

sections.label: Certificate Provider under England legislation
sections.summary: England and Wales legislation, which the Singapore MCA is modelled after, provides for a Certificate Provider and includes professional persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Legislation in England and Wales, of which the Singapore MCA is modelled after, provides for a "Certificate Provider" to be someone a donor knows well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I think that is a bit broad and general and I do not support that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But they also include professional persons such as one of the following: either a registered healthcare professional; a solicitor, barrister or advocate; a registered social worker; or an independent mental capacity advocate.

sections.label: Accreditation of social workers, psychologists
sections.summary: The speaker asks why certified, accredited social workers or psychologists cannot be accredited by the Public Guardian.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Why, for example, can certified, accredited social workers or psychologists not be accredited by the Public Guardian?

sections.label: Awareness of deputy appointment process
sections.summary: A process for application and appointment of deputies exists under the existing Act, but awareness of it remains low.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I understand that a process for the application and appointment for deputies has been put in place under the existing Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, the low level of awareness of the need and the process remains baffling to the main in the street.

sections.label: Resources for faster deputy process
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to allocate more financial resources and Ministry time for a faster process for those without mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They ought to urgently start the process of application and appointment, before it is too late.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge the Government to allocate more resources, both financial and for Ministry to allocate more time, to similarly enable a faster, customer-centric and effective process for those who are now without mental capacity.

sections.label: Notify Public Guardian before major decisions
sections.summary: Suggests making it mandatory for donees to notify the Public Guardian before exercising authority over major decisions affecting donors' living arrangements and finances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, Sir, I would like to suggest that it be made mandatory for donees to notify the Public Guardian of their intention to exercise their authority to make very major decisions on behalf of donors that impact the donor’s living arrangements and have major impact on their finances before doing so, so as to better safeguard persons who lack mental capacity from abuse.

sections.label: Guardian annual report and notification
sections.summary: Notes guardians must file annual reports and accounts, and suggests considering a basic requirement to notify the OPG of major donee decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The guardian must also file an annual report and provide accounting yearly as prescribed by the Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, a basic requirement to notify the OPG when a donee exercises their powers under the Act as regards to major financial and property-related decisions and major living arrangement-related decisions may be worth considering.

sections.label: Supported versus substituted decision-making models
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government would consider complementing the MCA's substituted decision-making model with a supported decision-making model in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lastly, Sir, for the longer-term evolution of this body of law and regulation, would the Government consider giving some thought to complementing a substitutive decision-making model for LPAs with a supported decision-making model in the future?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, the Mental Capacity Act or MCA adopts what can be termed a substituted decision-making model, which differs from the supported decision-making model now encouraged by the committee for the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities or CRPD.

sections.label: Supported decision-making in Canada and Sweden
sections.summary: Describes supported decision-making legal models in Canada's Manitoba and British Columbia and in Sweden, citing a paper by Devi, Bickenbach and Stucki.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As described in a paper by researchers Devi, Bickenbach and Stucki, Canada is one of the leading countries in the legal implementation of supported decision-making models, for example, the Vulnerable Persons Living with a Disability Act 1993 from the province of Manitoba.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another example is contained in the province of British Columbia's Representation Agreement Act (RAA), under which an adult can enter into a "representation agreement" with a trusted person or support service who is empowered to either to assist that individual in making and communicating certain decisions with which he or she needs assistance, or to make decisions for him or her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Sweden revoked its formal guardianship laws for adults with disabilities in 1989 and replaced it with this supported decision-making model.

sections.label: Supported decision-making as legal option
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government would consider developing instruments making supported decision-making a legal option donors can select alongside existing options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, in its Concluding Observations on Croatia and also General Comment No 1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I wonder, in conclusion, if the Government would give some thought to developing instruments in the future that would enable us to make supported decision-making a legal option that donors can select alongside the options currently provided for.

sections.label: Digitalising Lasting Power of Attorney process
sections.summary: States that the amendments debated will enable the Office of Public Guardian to digitalise the Lasting Power of Attorney process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The amendments we debate today will enable the Office of Public Guardian to digitalise the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) process.

sections.label: Public Guardian pre-LPA powers
sections.summary: Asks about legislative policy on the Public Guardian's role in safeguarding donors before an LPA is made, citing proposed amendments on interviewing donors and disclosing donee LPA numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I only have one short query and this is to clarify the legislative policy concerning the role of the Public Guardian in safeguarding the donor’s wellbeing and interests even before an LPA is made by him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This arises from the proposed amendments to give the Public Guardian (PG) the power to: (a) interview the donor if there are grounds to suspect there is fraud or undue influence to induce a donor to make an LPA or to appoint a particular person to be his donee; and (b) disclose to the donor the number of LPAs for which his prospective donee has already or will be appointed as donee on the same grounds.

sections.label: Expanding Public Guardian suitability checks
sections.summary: Asks why the Public Guardian's pre-registration role cannot extend beyond fraud and undue influence to cover the proposed donee's general suitability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My short query is in relation to why the role of the PG in safeguarding the donor’s interest before the registration of the LPA cannot be expanded beyond fraud and undue influence to also include general suitability of the proposed donee.

sections.label: Legislative intent limiting Public Guardian
sections.summary: Asks the Parliamentary Secretary to clarify the legislative intent in limiting the Public Guardian's role to suspected fraud or undue pressure on the donor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We know all too often how we shirk tasks that have high cognitive tax, such as reading the fine print of contracts and policies, and I am speaking as one who is paid to read fine print, even though I must admit I do this at work but not at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would be grateful if the hon Parliamentary Secretary could please clarify what is the legislative intent in circumscribing the PG’s role to just matters where it is suspected that fraud or undue pressure is used on the donor.

sections.label: Low LPA and Will uptake
sections.summary: Compares LPAs and Wills to health insurance, citing straw poll figures, about 100,000 LPAs registered by 2020, and slow coverage at 40,000 yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I thus believe that having an LPA or will done up to provide assurances in the event of the "ifs" and "what ifs" in life, is no less important than, say, the assurance of having basic health insurance plans in place, such as MediShield, for example, to which I note that with the rollout of MediShield Life in 2015, all Singaporeans are now covered for life, compared to 2.8 million policyholders back in 2006, notwithstanding the general population increase since then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I was thus a little sad and frankly unsurprised, however, that based on the straw poll that was conducted during our Zoom webinar, only 5% of participants have indicated that they have done up an LPA and 6% have done up a Will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Upon conducting further research, I note that up to 2020, there has only been about 100,000 LPAs registered in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if we exclude foreigners and base our calculations off the resident adult population of about 3.2 million people, the number of registered LPAs represent a mere 3.1% of the resident adult population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I recognise that MSF expects more than 40,000 LPAs to be registered by year-end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But even so, based on 40,000 LPAs registered a year, this will take the equivalent of about 80 years to get everyone covered; and most of us would not be here by then!

sections.label: LPA donor age and gender
sections.summary: States that from 2014 to 2019 most LPA donors were aged 50 and above, and female donors outnumbered male donors about 1.4 to one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Further, while I strongly believe that an LPA is important for adults of all ages, close to 80% of LPA donors from 2014 to 2019 are aged 50 and above, while 55% of LPA donors are aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Another interesting statistic which I observed is that from 2014 to 2019, female LPA donors have consistently outnumbered male LPA donors by a ratio of about 1.4 is to one.

sections.label: Digitised LPA registration time
sections.summary: States that once LPA is digitised, registration time will be shortened from three weeks to an average of eight working days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Once LPA is digitised, the time to register an LPA will be shortened from three weeks to an average of eight working days.

sections.label: Paper LPA form option
sections.summary: Speaker asks the Minister whether the paper LPA form can be kept, as with CPF nominations done online or at a service centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, it is nonetheless an online application form.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask the Minister if we can keep the paper form LPA , just like when we do CPF nominations, we can either do it online or go to the CPF Service Centre to fill up the physical form.

sections.label: What an LPA is
sections.summary: An LPA lets a donor voluntarily appoint donees to decide and act for him when he loses mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The LPA is a legal instrument which allows a person, the "donor", to voluntarily appoint one or more persons, the "donee", to make decisions and act on his behalf when he loses mental capacity one day.

sections.label: Residents completing LPAs
sections.summary: More than 300 residents have done up their LPAs in response to a special package and service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As of earlier this year, I know more than 300 residents have done up their LPAs in response to this special package and service for our residents.

sections.label: Certificate issuer charges support
sections.summary: Besides waiving the registration fee, support could include waiving or subsidising certificate issuer charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Besides waiver of the registration fee, which is a good move, support can come in the form of waiving or even subsidising the certificate issuer charges.

sections.label: Public Guardian fraud disclosure
sections.summary: Amendments propose letting the Public Guardian disclose to a donor that a prospective donee is already donee to multiple donors, and ask about exemptions and affected LPAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Further, the amendments propose to allow the Public Guardian, in case of suspected fraud, to disclose to a donor that his prospective donee is already a donee to multiple donors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Or would there be certain exemptions, for instance, where the appointed donee is either a next-of-kin, close relative, or friend of the multiple donors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Also, if the authorities suspect that fraud has been perpetrated, what will happen to all LPAs registered after the amendments have been passed?

sections.label: Safeguards for donors
sections.summary: The Public Guardian may interview the donor and disclose the number of LPAs the prospective donee was or intends to be appointed to.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: To provide additional safeguards for donors, it was mentioned that the Public Guardian may interview the donor and disclose to the donor the number of LPAs for which his or her prospective donee had already been appointed, or intends to be appointed.

sections.label: Disclosure, access and error correction
sections.summary: Asks for clarity on disclosure of non-confidential information, who may access it, access safeguards, and prompt notice of register corrections.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Regarding process robustness, for section 10B(1)(g) and section 46(2)(b) and (d), could more clarity be shared on (a) what circumstances and considerations would allow for the disclosure of this non-confidential information; (b) who would be allowed the access to this information and (c) will there be any measures in place to ensure that only those permitted have access to the information and that the risk of incorrect disclosure is minimised or even eliminated?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: On section 10D(1) and (3), in the event that the Public Guardian has to correct any error or omission in the register or document as a result of the malfunction of the electronic transaction system, would there be any prompt communication to inform both the donor and donee of the correction that has to be done?

sections.label: Electronic LPA filing costs
sections.summary: Asks whether donors will pay additional costs for electronic LPA filing compared with non-electronic LPA filing.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: With this move towards electronic LPAs, would there be any additional cost for the donor in the LPA filing as compared to the non-electronic LPA?

sections.label: Public Guardian rectification discretion
sections.summary: New section 11(10) lets the Public Guardian rectify a relevant error if satisfied one exists, suggesting discretion rather than obligation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 11(10) provides that the Public Guardian (PG) may rectify a relevant error if it is satisfied that there is a relevant error.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This suggests that the PG has the discretion to rectify a relevant error but is not obligated to rectify the error.

sections.label: Corrected errors and electronic copies
sections.summary: New sections 10D(3) and 16A(2) treat corrected errors as not having occurred and let good-faith transactors rely on electronic copies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new subsection 10D(3) provides that where an error or omission has been corrected, the error or omission is treated as not having occurred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new subsection 16A(2) provides that if an electronic copy of a non-electronic LPA has a relevant error, a person who transacts in good faith without knowing of the error is entitled to rely on the electronic copy for that transaction.

sections.label: Accessible support for online systems
sections.summary: Calls on the Government to provide accessible support systems for those daunted by online systems so they benefit from the initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While digitalisation is often intended to reduce burdens on manpower, we must be willing to cross the bridges with those whom we build it for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to make accessible support systems for those daunted by online systems in order for them to get the most out of this initiative.

sections.label: Mental capacity and online LPA services
sections.summary: Notes sporadic mental incapacities, online LPA convenience versus physical appointments, and the need to avoid doubt about pressure or mental impediments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Some conditions cause mental incapacities in bouts or sporadic episodes and cannot be recognised with certainty in one-off encounters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We recognise that online LPA services greatly add to the convenience of the process by reducing the need for physical appointments even though these physical appointments, arguably, play pivotal roles in the ascertainment of mental capacities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given the grave implications of making an LPA, we cannot, with good faith, proceed with the issuance of LPAs should there be any shadow of a doubt whether or not an individual is under pressure or has mental health impediments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We must get it right every single time.

sections.label: Online LPA safeguards and dementia
sections.summary: The speaker says online LPA issuance needs safeguards and evaluation, urges support for seniors crossing the digital divide, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Without additional safeguards or a transparent and rigorous evaluation system for mental capacity, the issuance of LPAs over an online system might become inconsistent at best, and, at worst, fail to protect the individuals it was precisely set out to protect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we necessarily lose the personal touch of the LPA process in introducing an online system, we must conscientiously support seniors in crossing the digital divide and intentionally build in safeguards that capture the diversity of our adults with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These concerns notwithstanding, Sir, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is very likely that each of us has a story to share about dementia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is part of life, because one in 10 aged 60 and above may have dementia.

sections.label: Safeguards against LPA fraud
sections.summary: The speaker asks for details on safeguards for process integrity and on measures and detection by the Public Guardian against fraud or undue pressure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary share further details on the safeguards that will be deployed to ensure the integrity of the process?

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: I also understand that in the event where there are grounds to suspect fraud or undue pressure used to induce a donor to make an LPA to appoint a particular person to be his or her donee, the Public Guardian may interview the donor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary share more on the measures in place and how the Office of the Public Guardian could have detected such occurrences and take swift action to safeguard the interest of the donor?

sections.label: Donees who are unrelated
sections.summary: Currently 90% of donees are immediate family members, leaving 10%, or about 2,100 donors in 2020, with unrelated donees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, 90% of donees are immediate family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Still, that leaves 10% of them, or about 2,100 donors in 2020 alone, who have unrelated donees.

sections.label: Checks and Mdm Chung case
sections.summary: Such checks may prevent fraud incidents like the 2016 Mdm Chung case, who appointed an unrelated former tour guide from China as donee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Having such checks may prevent fraud incidents like the high-profile Mdm Chung's case in 2016, who appointed an unrelated former tour guide from China as a donee.

sections.label: PAP Seniors Group LPA talks
sections.summary: Under PAP Seniors Group, LPA awareness talks will be rolled out to the public, encouraging more people, especially younger Singaporeans, to make their own LPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under PAP Seniors Group, we will be rolling out LPA awareness talks to the public, encouraging more people, especially younger Singaporeans, to make their own LPA.

sections.label: LPA versus ACP
sections.summary: Unlike the ACP, which is non-binding, an LPA is a legal document that appoints donees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Unlike the ACP, which is non-binding, an LPA is a legal document that appoints donees.

sections.label: MSF and MOH GP packages
sections.summary: MSF could work with MOH to encourage GPs, especially qualified CIs, to proactively provide LPA and ACP packages to patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: MSF could work with MOH to encourage all general practitioners (GPs), especially those who are concurrently qualified CIs, to proactively provide packages of LPA and ACP to their patients.

sections.label: LPA promotion and CPF nomination
sections.summary: MSF should offer LPAs to everyone above 30 and work with CPF Board on incorporating CPF nomination review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Offer LPAs to everyone who is above 30 years old, like CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: MSF should also work with CPF Board to see whether we can incorporate the process of reviewing one's nomination for CPF as well as LPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, it is encouraging for me to note that MSF will be expecting over 40,000 applications for Lasting Power of Attorney, or LPA, by the end of 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given that one in 10 Singaporeans aged 60 and above have the chance of being diagnosed with dementia, and with the numbers expected to rise to 80,000 in 2030, I believe that the LPA should be widely promoted to all Singaporeans as it allows an individual to make an early choice of a proxy decision-maker whom they can trust.

sections.label: LPA donors aged 60 and above
sections.summary: Since the LPA began in 2014, slightly more than half of donors are aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Since the inception of the LPA in 2014, slightly more than half of the donors are aged 60 years old and above.

sections.label: Section 16A e-LPA error protection
sections.summary: The Bill introduces section 16A, which protects donees and others if the e-LPA has a relevant error.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces section 16A that affords protection of donees and others if the e-LPA has a relevant error.

sections.label: New OPGO electronic system
sections.summary: One of the main amendments is to set up the new Office of the Public Guardian Online electronic system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One of the main amendments is to set up the new Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO) electronic system.

sections.label: SPF donor defrauding cases check
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it checked with the Singapore Police Force on the number of donor defrauding cases to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry share with the House if it had checked with the Singapore Police Force (SPF) on the number of cases involving the defrauding of donors to date?

sections.label: Sharing medical records with OPG
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether hospitals, IMH, MSF, MOH and OPG can share records securely and create a faster framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Instead of asking the aged home or caregiver to make an appointment to see the regular doctor for the sake of retrieving the medical record a few months later, would it not be much faster if the information can be shared between the Government restructured hospitals, including IMH, with OPG in a secured manner?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For the case which I had handled, I prayed that my client was able to outlive the Court order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, would the Government restructured hospitals, IMH, MSF, MOH as well as OPG work out a new framework to expedite this process?

sections.label: Digital LPA registration convenience
sections.summary: Speaker says digital shift brings convenience to donors and donees, with LPAs registered in eight working days instead of over three weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe it will bring much more convenience to both donors and donees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And with the shift to digital, LPAs can be registered in just eight working days, compared to the more than three weeks currently.

sections.label: MSF LPA adoption volume
sections.summary: MSF expects about 30,000 LPAs a year based on pre-COVID-19 trends, which the speaker calls too low and asks how wider adoption will be encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Going forward, MSF expects a transaction volume of around 30,000 LPAs to be made a year, based on pre-COVID-19 trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I think this is far too low a level of adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to ask how is MSF planning to encourage much wider adoption of LPAs?

sections.label: Mental Capacity Amendment Bill digitisation
sections.summary: MSF introduced the Mental Capacity (Amendment) Bill to digitise LPA making, cutting registration from three weeks to about eight working days and making LPAs electronic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   MSF introduced the Mental Capacity (Amendment) Bill to digitise the process of making a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Hence, the time taken to register an LPA will be shortened from three weeks to an average of eight working days, which is about half the current time needed, and the LPA itself will become an electronic document.

sections.label: Healthcare workers unprepared for death matters
sections.summary: Surveys show many healthcare workers have not prepared for death-related matters, including making an LPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Surveys have shown that even a large proportion of healthcare workers have not prepared for death-related matters, including making an LPA.

sections.label: Dementia risk and LPA touchpoints
sections.summary: Speaker says dementia probability after age 60 is closer to one in 10, and hopes MSF works with medical institutions to open more LPA touchpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In fact, the probability of getting dementia is not one in 10,000 but closer to one in 10 after the age of 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: With this, I hope that MSF will work with medical institutions to open up more LPA touchpoints.

sections.label: LPA donee and deputy options
sections.summary: States that a wife likely cannot act unless the husband had executed an LPA or she applies to Court to be appointed deputy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The answer to both of these questions is likely to be no, unless the husband had already executed the LPA and appointed his wife as his intended donee prior to becoming mentally incapacitated, or if the wife applies now to the Court to be officially appointed as her husband's deputy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The medical report required as part of the application process, as Mr Don Wee had shared earlier, would itself require at least another one to three months to obtain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Doing so will enable the applicant to have peace of mind while providing clarity and certainty to the applicants' families on who take up the role of donee should the applicant ever lose his mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I, therefore, applaud the latest move by MSF to establish an electronic transaction system to create new LPAs, as I believe that any reviews to make the process of registering an LPA more accessible and affordable are always welcome.

sections.label: Training officers for digital help
sections.summary: Suggests the agency consider training Silver Generation Officers and social workers who visit seniors' homes to assist with digital needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Whilst I note that the relevant agency intends to reach out to use community touchpoints, such as the Citizen Connect Centres in the Community Centres islandwide and the Integrated Public Service Centre at Our Tampines Hub, to assist people with digital needs to use the online service, I think that the relevant agency should also consider training our Silver Generation Officers and social workers who conduct regular house visits to seniors’ residences.

sections.label: My Legacy vault portal feature
sections.summary: Describes a beta portal's My Legacy vault, accessible via Singpass, letting users plan, store and share legal, healthcare and estate matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The portal, currently still in beta testing, has a My Legacy vault feature, which is accessible using Singpass, that allows users to plan, store and share legal, healthcare and estate matters securely with the people they trust.

sections.label: LPA Form 1 fee waiver
sections.summary: Notes the $75 LPA Form 1 fee waiver for Singaporeans is extended to 31 March 2023 and asks if registration fees could be removed entirely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Presently, the $75 application fee waiver for LPA Form 1 for Singaporeans has been extended to 31 March 2023, so as to encourage more Singaporeans to plan ahead and apply for an LPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is actually the fourth extension granted by the OPG since its first extension in 2016 and we would often see an influx in take-up rates when the waiver deadline draws close; this would inevitably cause the OPG backend to be stretched in terms of manpower while processing these new LPAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In light that the LPAs will now be digitalised, would the Ministry consider removing the registration fees for LPA Form 1 entirely?

sections.label: Donees informing OPG of incapacity
sections.summary: Proposes requiring donees to inform OPG and produce medical reports certifying donors lost mental capacity before exercising LPA powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If the medical report is not mandatory, I would like to propose to make it a requirement for donees to inform OPG and produce medical reports which certify that the donors have lost their mental capacities before the donees exercise the powers under the LPAs.

sections.label: Donee statutory declaration option
sections.summary: Suggests alternatively requiring the donee to submit a Statutory Declaration confirming a doctor certified the donor lacks mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Alternatively, the donee can be required to submit a Statutory Declaration to confirm that the donor has been certified by a doctor to lack mental capacity.

sections.label: Limit on donee appointments
sections.summary: Suggests considering a limit on the maximum number of LPAs on which someone can be appointed as a donee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, perhaps, it would be useful to consider a limit on the maximum number of LPAs on which someone can be appointed as a donee.

sections.label: OPG database for donee changes
sections.summary: Asks whether a database or system exists for OPG updates when a donee ceases to be a family member or predeceases the donor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, may I ask if there is a database or system for OPG to be updated once the donee on an LPA ceases to be a family member, by virtue of divorce or has predeceased the donor?

sections.label: LPA registration numbers rise
sections.summary: States about 8,000 LPAs were registered in 2016, over 9,000 in the first three months of 2021, and MSF expects over 40,000 by year end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In 2016, there were only about 8,000 LPAs registered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But in just the first three months of 2021, we have seen over 9,000 LPAs registered and MSF expects more than 40,000 LPAs to be registered by the end of this year.

sections.label: Electronic LPA error rectification period
sections.summary: Under the Bill, an electronic copy of a registered LPA is treated as free from error if no rectification is notified to OPG within 90 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, the electronic copy of a registered LPA will be treated as free from error if individuals do not notify the OPG of any rectification within 90 days.

sections.label: Outreach channels and fraud safeguards
sections.summary: Suggests using regional Social Service Offices for outreach to vulnerable Singaporeans, ensuring less tech-savvy access and robust safeguards against fraud.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We can also consider using the regional Social Service Office to be used as another channel to outreach to vulnerable Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But we need to ensure that the less tech-savvy have easy access to the process and there must be robust safeguards to prevent fraud.

sections.label: Electronic copies superseding hard copy LPAs
sections.summary: States the hard copy LPA will no longer be treated by law as the LPA once the electronic copy is treated as such by operation of law.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As to whether the electronic copies will supersede the hard copy LPAs, the hard copy LPA will no longer be treated by the law as the LPA after the electronic copy is treated by the operation of law as such.

sections.label: Electronic copy becomes LPA
sections.summary: The electronic copy becomes the LPA after 90 days if no relevant error is reported, or later if an error is reported.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The electronic copy only becomes the LPA after the 90-day period if no relevant error is spotted and reported.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: If a relevant error is reported to OPG, the electronic copy becomes the LPA either on the 91st day or on the day which the Public Guardian rectifies the relevant error, whichever is later.

sections.label: Protection for donees and third parties
sections.summary: New section 16A protects donees relying on the electronic copy and third parties transacting in good faith without knowing of a relevant error.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The new section 16A of the MCA, which is inserted by clause 10 of the Bill, protects donees who have acted in reliance on the electronic copy without knowing of the relevant error and third parties who have transacted in good faith without knowing of the relevant error.

sections.label: 90-day cut-off gives certainty
sections.summary: The 90-day cut-off provides certainty in the LPA's status and allows confident transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Thirdly, the 90-day cut-off provides certainty in the LPA's status and allows confident transactions.

sections.label: Confidential information access and objections
sections.summary: Subsidiary legislation will restrict LPA information access, and under new section 33A the Public Guardian must not rectify if a non-frivolous objection is made.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Second, on whether access to confidential information contained in the LPA will be restricted – subsidiary legislations will be amended such that only donors, donees and transacting third parties authorised by the donor or donee may access this information.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Third, on the next steps should a donee or donor object to the proposed rectification or update of the Public Guardian's register – under the new section 33A of the Act, which is inserted by clause 14 of the Bill, the Public Guardian must not proceed with the rectification or updating if the person objects unless the Public Guardian is satisfied that the objection is frivolous, vexatious or has been withdrawn.

sections.label: OPGO system outage recovery
sections.summary: OPGO runs across multiple zones, and after a system outage it is expected to be restored and tested within a reasonable timeframe, possibly a day.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: OPGO will run across these multiple zones to provide better infrastructure resilience and scalability for business operations.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Thus, in the unlikely event of a system outage, we expect OPGO to be restored and tested within a reasonable timeframe, possibly within a day, so that users can continue their LPA applications by the next day.

sections.label: Certificate for personal welfare transactions
sections.summary: Clause 7 amends section 13(10) to let transacting parties require donees to produce a certificate for transactions involving the donor's personal welfare.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Clause 7 of the Bill will amend section 13(10) of the MCA to also enable transacting parties to require donees to produce such a certificate for transactions involving the donor’s personal welfare.

sections.label: OPGO donee capacity declaration
sections.summary: The OPGO process requires the donee to declare on OPGO that the donor has lost mental capacity before transacting using the LPA.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The OPGO process will also address some of the Members’ concerns, namely, the donee will need to declare on OPGO that the donor has lost mental capacity before transacting using the LPA.

sections.label: Alert on multiple doneeships
sections.summary: The system will alert the Public Guardian if a prospective donee has been appointed as donee in multiple LPAs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The system will alert the Public Guardian if any prospective donee has been appointed as donee in multiple LPAs.

sections.label: Public Guardian seeks Court directions
sections.summary: With evidence of fraud or undue pressure, the Public Guardian may seek the Court's directions under section 17 of the MCA on registering the LPA.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, should the Public Guardian have evidence of fraud or undue pressure, she may seek the Court’s directions under existing section 17 of the MCA on whether the LPA should be registered.

sections.label: Donees are trusted family members
sections.summary: Over 95% of donees are trusted family members chosen by donors, and multiple doneeships are not uncommon.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With more than 95% of donees being trusted family members who are chosen by donors themselves, we agree with Ms Sylvia Lim that multiple doneeships are not uncommon.

sections.label: Public Guardian investigates donee abuse
sections.summary: Donors should appoint trusted donees, but if a donee abuses his or her powers, the Public Guardian may investigate and apply to Court to revoke the LPA.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: It is important that donors appoint donees whom they trust.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: But in the rare case where a donee abuses his or her powers, the Public Guardian is empowered to investigate the case and may apply to the Court under the existing section 17 of the MCA to revoke the LPA.

sections.label: Simplified deputyship application savings
sections.summary: Many cases have benefited from the time and cost savings arising from the simplified deputyship application track.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Many cases have benefited from the time and cost savings arising from the simplified deputyship application track.

sections.label: Certificate Issuers on OPG website
sections.summary: Singaporeans may refer to OPG's website for the list of more than 7,000 Certificate Issuers.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Currently, Singaporeans may refer to OPG’s website for the list of more than 7,000 Certificate Issuers.

sections.label: No extra cost for electronic LPA
sections.summary: No additional costs are incurred when making an LPA electronically, and the LPA Form 1 application fee waiver for Singaporeans is extended to 31 March 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: First, there will be no additional costs incurred when making an LPA electronically.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We have extended the LPA Form 1 application fee waiver for Singaporeans to 31 March 2023.

sections.label: Top doctors' charges
sections.summary: As at January this year, the majority of the top 10 most visited doctors charged $50 or less, especially for senior citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As at January this year, the majority of the top 10 most visited doctors charged $50 or less, especially for senior citizens.

sections.label: Donors below age 50
sections.summary: Since 2010, there are about 30,000 donors below the age of 50.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Since 2010, we have about 30,000 donors below the age of 50.

sections.label: Registered LPA numbers
sections.summary: From 346 registered LPAs in 2010, more than 20,000 LPAs were registered in the first six months of this year alone.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From just 346 registered LPAs in 2010, we now have more than 20,000 LPAs registered just in the first six months of this year alone.
